definitions.explanation: Living to an old age; having a long lifespan. Used both as a noun describing longevity and as a na-adjective describing someone or something that is long-lived.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖母|そぼ}→祖母：00813_sobo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{長命|ちょうめい}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧95⟦{歳|さい}→歳：10017_sai⟧⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧⟦{生|い}きた→生きる：01184_ikiru⟧。
examples.english: My grandmother was long-lived and lived to 95.

examples.japanese: {長命|ちょうめい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{秘訣|ひけつ}→秘訣：13750_hiketsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{何|なん}→何〜：03100_nan⟧です⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧。
examples.english: What is the secret to a long life?

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{世界|せかい}→世界：01447_sekai⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧{長命|ちょうめい}な⟦{国|くに}→国：02204_kuni⟧⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{知|し}られて→知る：00458_shiru⟧おり、⟦{食生活|しょくせいかつ}→食生活：21071_shokuseikatsu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦その→その：00993_sono⟧⟦{要因|よういん}→要因：05581_youin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{一|ひと}つ→一つ：02948_hitotsu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われている→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: Japan is known as one of the most long-lived countries in the world, and diet is said to be one of the factors.

notes:
Composed of {長|ちょう} (long) + {命|めい} (life). A somewhat literary word for longevity. In everyday conversation, ⟦{長生|ながい}き→長生き：03128_nagaiki⟧ is more common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {長命|ちょうめい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{秘訣|ひけつ}→秘訣：13750_hiketsu⟧: the secret to longevity
- {長命|ちょうめい}な⟦{家系|かけい}→家系：10130_kakei⟧: a long-lived family line
- {長命|ちょうめい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{祈|いの}る→祈る：01198_inoru⟧: to pray for a long life

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{長生|ながい}き→長生き：03128_nagaiki⟧: long life — the most common everyday word for living long
- ⟦{長寿|ちょうじゅ}→長寿：14478_chouju⟧: longevity — slightly more formal, often used in celebrations and statistics
- ⟦{寿命|じゅみょう}→寿命：12359_jumyou⟧: lifespan — the expected length of life, not necessarily long

REGISTER:
Slightly literary or formal. More often encountered in writing, proverbs, and traditional expressions than in casual speech.
